title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
one_liner: Demonstrated that pure RL with GRPO can unlock PhD-level mathematical reasoning without supervised fine-tuning.
problem: Frontier reasoning models (e.g. OpenAI o1) were closed-source and relied heavily on massive proprietary human-annotated chain-of-thought demonstrations.
breakthrough: Trained DeepSeek-R1-Zero directly via pure Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) using accuracy and formatting rewards, discovering self-verification, reflection, and lengthy chain-of-thought exploration natively.
impact: Democratized frontier reasoning globally and established GRPO as the new benchmark for post-training reasoning models.

title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-Precision
authors: Jay Shah, Ganesh Bikshandi, Ying Zhang, Vijay Thakkar, Pradeep Ramani, Tri Dao
one_liner: Exploited NVIDIA Hopper asynchronous Tensor Cores and FP8 precision to reach up to 1.2 PFLOPs/s attention throughput.
problem: Standard attention algorithms failed to saturate newer GPU architectures like NVIDIA H100 Hopper due to memory synchronization overhead and non-overlapping GEMM vs. Softmax pipelines.
breakthrough: Introduced Producer-Consumer warp specialization, asynchronous Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) pipelining, and block-quantized FP8 attention with online scaling.
impact: Enables 1M+ token context windows to train and infer at near-hardware limit speeds on modern datacenter GPUs.

title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
one_liner: Proved theoretical equivalence between Selective State Space Models and Linear Attention via Structured State Space Duality (SSD).
problem: While Mamba-1 provided $O(N)$ linear inference, it could not leverage high-throughput GPU Tensor Cores optimized for matrix-matrix multiplication (GEMM).
breakthrough: Unveiled SSD framework connecting SSM recurrence to semiseparable 1-semiseparable matrix multiplication, allowing block-level parallel matrix math at 8x faster training throughput.
impact: Bridges the gap between attention-based LLMs and linear RNNs, powering next-generation hybrid architectures like Jamba and Nemotron.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models: Technical Report
one_liner: Trained 405B parameter dense Transformer on 15T multilingual tokens across a 16K H100 GPU cluster.
problem: Open-weight models lagged behind proprietary closed models (GPT-4) in reasoning, coding, and multilingual translation capabilities.
breakthrough: Standard dense autoregressive decoder architecture scaled to 405B parameters with Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), 128k context window, and multi-stage alignment involving iterative rejection sampling and DPO.
impact: Serves as the foundational open backbone for thousands of fine-tuned research models and synthetic data generation.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn
one_liner: Mathematically derived an exact closed-form objective to align LLMs with human preferences without training a separate reward model or RL loop.
problem: PPO reinforcement learning from human feedback is notorious for training instability, hyperparameter brittleness, and extreme GPU memory overhead.
breakthrough: Reparametrized the Bradley-Terry reward function directly in terms of the optimal policy's implicit log-likelihood ratio relative to a reference model.
impact: Replaced PPO in the vast majority of modern LLM alignment pipelines (Zephyr, Mistral, Llama, Gemma).

title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (DiT)
one_liner: Replaced the standard U-Net backbone in diffusion models with pure Transformers, establishing predictable scaling laws for generative vision.
problem: U-Net convolutional backbones lacked standardized compute-scaling properties that enabled large language models to scale predictably.
breakthrough: Tokenized image latents into spatial patches and applied adaptive layer normalization (adaLN-Zero) conditioning inside standard Transformer blocks.
impact: The foundational vision architecture behind OpenAI Sora, Stable Diffusion 3, Flux, and Runway Gen-3.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
authors: Tim Dettmers, Artidoro Pagnoni, Ari Holtzman, Luke Zettlemoyer
one_liner: Made it possible to fine-tune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU without performance degradation.
problem: Full 16-bit fine-tuning of 65B models required >780GB of GPU VRAM across multi-node clusters, locking out independent researchers.
breakthrough: Introduced 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization optimal for normally distributed weights, Double Quantization, and Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes.
formula: $$W^{\text{Dequant}} = \text{dequantize}(c_1, c_2, W^{\text{NF4}}), \quad Y = W^{\text{Dequant}} X + \frac{\alpha}{r} B A X$$
impact: Enabled consumer-grade GPUs to fine-tune enterprise-grade LLMs, democratizing open-source AI tuning.

title: ColBERTv2: Effective and Efficient Retrieval via Lightweight Token Inversion
authors: Keshav Santhanam, Omar Khattab, Christopher Potts, Matei Zaharia
one_liner: Achieved state-of-the-art dense retrieval quality with 6-10x compression via multi-vector token late interaction.
problem: Single-vector bi-encoders (e.g. OpenAI ada-002) compress entire documents into one point, suffering catastrophic loss of fine-grained entity detail.
breakthrough: Retained per-token contextual vectors and computed similarity using MaxSim sum over token dot products, compressed with residual quantization.
impact: Underpins modern high-precision RAG engines, providing token-level interpretability and superior retrieval on complex multi-hop queries.

title: The Era of 1-bit LLMs: All Large Language Models are in 1.58 Bits
authors: Shuming Ma, Hongyu Wang, Lingxiao Shen, Ting Song, Furu Wei
one_liner: Demonstrated that ternary weights {-1, 0, 1} match 16-bit LLM perplexity while eliminating floating-point matrix multiplications entirely.
problem: Dense matrix multiplications (FP16/BF16) consume massive electrical power and memory bandwidth in GPU tensor cores.
breakthrough: Proposed BitLinear layer where weights are constrained to ternary values $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, replacing expensive matrix multiplication with integer addition.
impact: Unlocks orders-of-magnitude energy and memory reductions for edge devices and future custom non-silicon accelerators.

title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
one_liner: Combined interleaved sliding window local attention, soft logit capping, and post-pretraining knowledge distillation in 9B and 27B weights.
problem: Small LLMs (2B-9B) suffered from training instability and high inference latency when running full attention over long sequences.
breakthrough: Interleaved sliding window attention with global attention every alternating layer, and applied soft logit capping to prevent gradient explosions without clipping.
impact: Delivered GPT-3.5-class reasoning capabilities at single-GPU footprint, setting an efficiency benchmark for open enterprise deployment.

title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
authors: Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Tao Xu, Greg Brockman, Christine McLeavey, Ilya Sutskever
one_liner: Trained encoder-decoder Transformer on 680,000 hours of multilingual web audio to approach human-level zero-shot transcription robustness.
problem: Traditional ASR systems overfitted to clean benchmark distributions (e.g. LibriSpeech) and failed in noisy real-world environments.
breakthrough: Trained an end-to-end sequence-to-sequence model using multi-task conditioning tokens that simultaneously perform language identification, voice activity detection, and translation.
impact: Became the global standard for universal audio transcription, speech-to-text pipelines, and voice interfaces.

title: Search-at-Test-Time and Process Reward Models for Frontier Mathematical Reasoning
one_liner: Proved that allocating compute at test-time via tree search and step-level PRMs scales reasoning power exponentially.
problem: Outcome reward models (ORMs) only evaluate final answers, giving positive feedback to flawed reasoning that accidentally arrived at the right number.
breakthrough: Trained step-by-step Process-Supervised Reward Models (PRMs) to score individual thought steps, enabling Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) exploration at inference time.
impact: Unlocked the System-2 reasoning paradigm (OpenAI o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1), proving test-time compute can substitute for pre-training scale.
